As I've mentioned in a couple of other articles today, Amazon has recently restocked a whole bunch of rare Pokémon TCG sets for Labor Day , and there are some hot goods up for grabs right now if you're fast enough.

Scarlet & Violet—Prismatic Evolutions Super-Premium Collection is now available again and in stock at Amazon for $274.99. The listed median price for these is around $310, according to TCGplayer , so at $274.99, you're getting a fairly good price (albeit still well above MSRP).

The market price is a little lower at around $257.54 , meaning you could potentially save a few bucks by buying through the resale market on TCGplayer or eBay. Just remember that those prices don't necessarily include delivery, so the gap can narrow pretty quickly.

Amazon is still a solid option if you've got some credit or gift cards burning a hole in your account, or if you'd rather have the peace of mind of buying a brand-new, guaranteed-sealed box directly from a major retailer instead of a third-party seller.

But why is Prismatic Evolutions still so popular for collectors and general players? The Scarlet & Violet set is still monunmentally popular, and goes from strength to strength, pretty much because of its hot card pull potential.

When these sets can potentially bag you a $1500 ultra rare, such as Umbreon ex - 161/131 ( the most valuable card from last year ) sometimes the high cost is considered worth it. I'm not entirely convinced myself, as after buying more than a few of these, you're halfway there to just buying the pricey card outright anyway.
Still! If you think these will bounce up in value further, you could always pick up one to open, and another to keep as an investment to see how it appreciates in value in the future.

Unfortunately, finding Pokémon TCG products at MSRP has become increasingly difficult, and market prices are often what collectors are forced to pay, even when buying from major retailers like Amazon.

As I mentioned, there are a few other notable Pokémon TCG restocks at Amazon right now, including the First Partner Illustration Collection Series 3 sets for $34, and Destined Rivals ETBs for $125.
Both the Destined Rivals ETBs and First Partner Collections are also roughly in line with current market prices, so you're not paying a huge premium to pick them up from Amazon right now.

2026 is a huge year for Pokémon TCG . The biggest expansion on the horizon is the monumental Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration expansion, launching globally on September 16, 2026.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/09/07/header-1788811440204.jpg

In case you missed it, Magic: The Gathering has returned to Middle-Earth with some gusto. The Lord of the Rings set is widely regarded as one of the best Universes Beyond offerings yet, and The Hobbit is getting a pretty great reception from players, too.
As the set only launched recently, its Collector Boosters are harder to find than the Arkenstone in Smaug’s hoard of treasures, but Amazon has a “deal” that might get your attention.
There Is A Catch, Depending On Where You Stand
We say “deal” because, as with many things with this set right now, the Magic: The Gathering Hobbit Gift bundle is being sold for more than its MSRP.
In fact, Wizards says it should be $89.99, so $164 is a colossal price hike. And yet, the same bundle can be found for $200 elsewhere, or is simply sold out with no sign of returning.

We’re giving you this information up front because you’re a big Hobbit now and you can spend your money as you please, but this is still a discount of 18% on the same bundle purchased elsewhere. If you really want it, buy it; if you don’t want to spend that kind of money, we get it, but at least you’re informed.

So what’s the big draw? While it is true that you get 9 Play Boosters inside, the most valuable cards in the set are restricted to Collector Boosters. And in this bundle, you’ll find one (hopefully to rule them all).
Smaug? Bard? Gandalf? What’ll it be? Well, that’s the point, really: you could open a whole bunch of neat rare cards, or you could pay your next month’s rent by pulling a Gleaming Splendor.

Aside from the ten total packs, you’ll also get 34 land cards that include full-art seasonal Hobbit lands that are exclusive to this set, and 10 full-art Middle-Earth Journey lands (honestly, these are so cool I’d probably frame them). There’s also a die inside and a box to keep everything in.

others.title: 《极限竞速：地平线 6》开发者重申 2026 年发布 PS5 版本

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/05/15/forza-main-1778862653522.jpg
Forza Horizon 6 is still planned to launch on PS5 this year, despite not having a firm release date yet.

Playground Games has confirmed it still plans to release Forza Horizon 6 on PS5 this year, following rumors that it might be delayed . Nothing else was shared about the port, but the clock is ticking for this new version.

"If you’re planning your trip to Discover Japan on PlayStation 5, stay tuned!" Playground said in a post today. "Forza Horizon 6 will be releasing on PS5 later this year, and you can add the game to your Wishlist on the PlayStation Store to be notified of availability."

September and October are loaded with big releases like Marvel's Wolverine and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , but there is enough difference in the audiences for these respective titles for Forza Horizon 6 to still succeed. November, however, is a different story. Launching Forza Horizon 6 on PS5 in November seems like a death wish given GTA 6 is set to dominate the industry upon its release. GTA 6 is expected to have an in-depth car customization system and races in addition to all of the other features one expects from GTA, making it hard to imagine players choosing Forza over GTA.

December may be more feasible, though the GTA 6 hype will still be very high and a hot item for the holiday season. It's hard to say, but Microsoft and Playground don't have too much time to build up to the PS5 release. Forza Horizon 5 was a massive hit on PlayStation 5, despite coming to the platform very late, so players will be attracted to it regardless.

Forza Horizon 6 is one of the biggest games of 2026 , which has been a very busy year for gaming. It's one of the best-selling games of the year and has garnered a ton of critical praise, including from IGN , which gave the game a 10/10.

"Technically, Forza Horizon 6 has not skipped a beat, and it runs like a titan," an excerpt from our review said. "Aesthetically, it’s the best-looking and best-sounding game Playground has produced to date, set in the most wonderfully realised map it’s ever crafted – full of dense, authentic details and stunning driving roads. It’s rewarding to explore, the campaign is well-paced with a great payoff, and I simply cannot stop playing."

content.v: The fidelity of Grand Theft Auto 6's world makes random violence look considerably less silly than it did when the characters had boxy claws for hands, but Rockstar isn't stopping players from doing what they want in Vice City and its environs.

We know that because we've seen the GTA 6 leaker shoot up a nudist party, murder the residents of a homeless encampment, and beat a delivery driver to death—quite a contrast with the mission-focused gameplay in the official reveal .

A little devil icon in one of the leaked videos did lead us to wonder if GTA 6 might judge us for pursuing violent chaos, a la Red Dead Redemption 2's Honor system, but details about GTA 6's 'Criminal Profiles' suggest that it isn't quite like that.

According to a preview from TGG on YouTube (embedded above), Rockstar doesn't want to punish players for how they play, or create a situation where they have to grind their reputation up to a 'better' level in order to progress.
Here's the short version of what TGG learned on his trip to Rockstar North:

This all aligns with IGN's learnings , but adds a few new specifics. What neither source came away with are specifics about how or how much Criminal Profiles will affect the story—will it lead to different endings, or just slightly change how NPCs interact with us?—but a comment from GTA 6 co-studio head Rob Nelson suggests that we will notice the effects of our actions.
Asked what he's most proud of in GTA 6, Nelson told TGG that it's "the way the whole thing works together."

"We've got a lot of very complicated systems working in an interconnected way," said Nelson. "You can forget it's a game that has been designed to try and work this way. I think it allows you to sort of roleplay as heavily or as lightly as you want to.

"The idea that you have a fair amount of choice now in terms of the way you can approach situations. You can still cause as much carnage as you can imagine. How does that make you feel if it has an impact on certain things? Do you still want to do it? Do you want to do it more? Do you want to do it less? Do you care at all? It's up to you and what matters to you."

items.title: 《GTA 6》是否过于现实而不利于其本身？汽车加油和枪支限制引发争论
items.summary: Early Grand Theft Auto 6 details have sparked debate about whether Rockstar Games' latest is too realistic for

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/31/hrdxhdzwwaax1k-1788198129736.jpg
Early Grand Theft Auto 6 details have sparked debate about whether Rockstar Games' latest is too realistic for its own good.

We've learned a lot about GTA 6 since its big extended look reveal. While the 13-year wait for Jason and Lucia's story already seems worth it for some, others fear Rockstar has taken its commitment to realistic gameplay a bit too seriously when it comes to its new open-world video game.

The studio is known for packing its games with details that fans could spend years combing through – and for better or worse, GTA 6 seems no different. Co-development lead Rob Nelson promised as much during a recent interview with content creator TGG . One element where the new Grand Theft Auto will differ from its predecessor involves how NPCs react to guns, with Nelson teasing that you can't just wander around with an RPG and expect zero pushback.

"The reactions are much more nuanced than before," he said. "So, if you've got a long gun on your back, you should be fine. If you've got one in your hand, people don't like it, and they react and start moving away from you. The more guns you carry and the way you carry them matters.
"If cops see you they will give you a warning. If you hold a long arm in both hands as though you are ready to fire it, things begin to escalate."

It certainly sounds more Red Dead Redemption 2 than Grand Theft Auto 5. Fans generally feel the 2013 GTA game thrives on mayhem, whereas the 2018 cowboy simulator found strength in its quiet, grounded moments. Nelson admitted that, in 2026, times have changed, explaining that Rockstar didn't "feel that works any longer at this resolution – with the behavioral sophistication we need from our population now."
"In GTA 5 you can pull out a shotgun from nowhere in front of people and they don't react," he elaborated. "That doesn't work here."

Even a slight shift toward a more realistic Vice City is something fans have expected from GTA 6 for some time, but that doesn't make Nelson's comments any less worth discussing. Should Rockstar lean on the cartoonish chaos GTA is known for, or sprinkle in the realism that made RDR2 special? That's the question many have found themselves asking the last few days.
"Next this game will make you file tax returns," one fan joked .
"I'm here for as full of an immersion as they can make," another argued , "RDR2 is the best game I've ever played and I love that they are making GTA 6 more like it."
Other fans fall somewhere in the middle, with one Reddit user pointing out that "At the point I pull out a gun I’m probably gonna do something worse than brandishing so this is fine."
remember carrying c4, rpgs, molotovs and like 10 guns at once in gta5 those days are over 😓
When does a video game stop being a video game

Rockstar is surely keenly aware of the balancing act it needs to pull off, but that didn't stop it from adding in more realistic elements. One mechanic present in other open-world sandbox games that will make its GTA debut in November will ask players to keep an eye on their car's gas. Yes, really.

In what leans more into the realism department, Nelson confirmed to TGG in a separate video that gas stations will allow players to repair and even refuel their vehicles. The YouTuber said filling up your car "typically isn't very expensive" and takes only about 10 seconds to do. It's no surprise to hear Rockstar already anticipated players being a bit torn when it asked players to bring car chases to a halt with a quick pitstop.
"That's pretty fast for a fill up," Nelson said when getting gas during TGG's preview event. "You can't complain about that!"
GTA 6 fans have, in fact, complained about that.

So in GTA 6 I have to: -eat -sleep -go to the gym -nurture my relationship -fill up my car with gas Isn’t the entire point of a video game to do things you can’t do in real life? This ultra-realism shit sounds exhausting
imagine seeing this in gta6 pic.twitter.com/E4RJ6AKHl1

I love that they added refueling to GTA 6 Imagine being chased by the cops and then suddenly your gas runs out near the swamps, so now you have to ditch the car and run through the swamps, dodging alligators AND cops. It's gonna result in so many unique gameplay moments! pic.twitter.com/87XIX6OpsC
"Oh I can complain buddy," one Reddit user said . "I don't even know anything about this and I'm complaining already."

"It should make gameplay more interesting: you steal a car, run out of gas, have to continue on foot, try to find a gas station, or a new ride," another theorized . "More variation than driving indefinitely until you crash or escape. I'm into it."

"If I can’t pull up, standing their filling up whilst complaining about the price, then go inside to pay, standing behind someone who is buying 15 different chocolate bars and a s**tload of scratch cards then I don’t wanna play this realism simulator game!" one fan joked .

Rockstar's desire to drop players into a realistic Vice City extends beyond a few new gameplay mechanics and features. This version of the Miami-inspired sandbox will also feature what is promised to be the most realistic map players have explored in the series thus far. With more lifelike guns and characters comes potentially more realistic romance options , too. Some couples have reported that falling in love with Jason or Lucia, or heading to an in-game strip club, is grounds for a real-life break-up . Ouch.

But wait, there's more! GTA 6 will also track how Jason and Lucia are getting along in Vice City, including whether they've gotten enough beauty sleep in between heists. Nelson told TGG that players know whether the protagonists are well-rested enough, with sleep able to affect "regens of certain attributes." One mechanic Rockstar eventually cut for being too realistic would have had players purchasing groceries to restock their refrigerator.

"We are always trying to find the right balance between realism and ease of play," Nelson told Famitsu (translation by GamesRadar ). "Rather than just going to the fridge to grab a snack or visiting a restaurant just to roleplay, we want to give meaning to each action."

GTA 6 has (predictably) kicked up discourse months before its November 19 release date for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S. That said, when it comes to the realistic elements in the game, one Reddit user nicely summed up how most will actually feel when they get their hands on the full release: "Just hope they remember to put the fun in. Realism is great, but if it's too tedious it'll be a bummer."

We'll know just how realistic gun restrictions, strip clubs, and fuel tanks will be when GTA 6 launches in a few months. While we wait, be sure to read up on IGN's interview and preview . You can also learn about the new PS5 controllers Rockstar announced last week.

items.summary: Rockstar will launch Grand Theft Auto 6 at midnight local time in most countries on November 19 — meaning some

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/06/gtaonothumb-1786018055324.png
Rockstar will launch Grand Theft Auto 6 at midnight local time in most countries on November 19 — meaning some fans are already planning to adjust their console region and play early.
Rather than offering a fixed time worldwide, the midnight local rollout means players in New Zealand will get a roughly 20-hour headstart on Mexico and elsewhere in Central America.

Of course, there are no GTA 6 discs to get started with early — even though Rockstar's long-awaited release will arrive as an entirely single-player experience. While pre-loading will be available, the game itself will not unlock until your timezone's allotted window.

Timestamps spotted on the PlayStation Store by GTAVice show 15 major release times for GTA 6 across the world's various timezones, beginning in New Zealand at 11am UTC on November 18, which is midnight on November 19 for our Kiwi friends.

If you're playing on Xbox Series X/S and want to adjust your console setting, this will be your earliest opportunity to play. If you have a PlayStation 5, this trick doesn't work — though you could technically play early with a separate New Zealand account, funded via a New Zealand gift card. (I guess this is one way GTA 6 actually plays better on Xbox .)

After New Zealand, the game's rollout then continues through timezones in Australia, Japan, India, through mainland Europe to the U.K., then to the U.S. — though at least here, all the country will get to play at midnight Eastern. So, if you're on the west coast, you'll get a few extra hours to play before bedtime (if you actually plan on going to sleep).

As a reminder, GTA 6 launches on November 19, just 72 days away. If you've preordered the game, you'll be able to start pre-loading from November 12, which is also when boxed copies (containing a digital download code) will ship. Rockstar is yet to say how much free space you'll need to get the game installed, but keep an eye on IGN for all of the details you'll need.

items.summary: Onimusha: Way of the Sword's launch day success has propelled the series to 10 million lifetime sales, says Ca

content.v: Samurai adventure Onimusha: Way of the Sword notched over a million sales on its launch day, Capcom has announced.

The success is deserved, per our reviewer Wes, who said that Way of the Sword "whips ass" in his 83/100 review . (And if the demo had you worried that it wouldn't be much of a challenge, Wes says not to fret too much: "I died plenty, particularly to bosses that ruthlessly punished my poor parry timing or overeager button mashing.")

According to Capcom, the one million launch day sales for Way of the Sword has put the Onimusha series as a whole at 10 million lifetime sales. The last new game in the main series was Onimusha: Dawn of Dreams, which released 20 years ago.

"In addition to regularly releasing major new titles each year, Capcom is focusing on re-activating IPs that haven't had a new title launch recently," the developer said. "The company is working to further maximize corporate value by leveraging its rich library of content, including this title."
New Lost Planet game when?

It's become a cliche to say that Capcom's on a bit of a run lately, but here's yet another mile marker in the developer's successful 2020s, which have included a pair of well-liked Resident Evil remakes, two new Resident Evil games, Monster Hunter Rise and Wilds, Pragmata, Street Fighter 6, and Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess, among other games.

items.title: OpenAI 在首次发现德国“维基事件”几周后公开承认这一事件
items.summary: Back on track?

content.v: OpenAI has officially acknowledged the 'wiki incident,' which involved a number of the company's AI agents breaking containment and hijacking an obscure German website.

The AI agents had been tasked with looking up something online, though originally did not have the ability to write anything outside of the testing environment. But as far back as May, the AI agents bypassed OpenAI's security measures, hijacked the communally editable German webpage, and began using it like a forum, trading tips on how to cheat on tests. Researchers first drew wider attention to the agents' 'forum' on September 4 .

OpenAI now says it needs to be more transparent about when its agents 'go rogue', writing on X , "It’s past time for us to define standards for when and how we share misalignment incidents, not just misalignment properties of our models."

The company had known about the 'misaligned' rogue behaviour for weeks before writing this post, according to Reuters , though only acknowledged the incident publicly this past Saturday. This statement follows shortly after the agentic attack on Hugging Face's servers .

"Historically, we have treated misalignment largely as a research question, which gets communicated in research publications such as systems cards," OpenAI writes. "This year, we’ve started to see misalignment cause new types of real-world impact."

To recap, 'misalignment' broadly describes rogue AI behaviour; an AI is 'misaligned' when it pursues goals that diverge from human intents or values—such as deleting your entire email inbox when you very much did not tell the AI agent to do that . It's a soft word for AI behaviour that could have serious consequences.

OpenAI says it did not communicate publicly about the 'wiki' incident specifically because the company felt it was similar to other instances of "agents using the internet in unintended ways" that it had already shared. The Hugging Face incident has caused the company to re-evaluate more than just its comms approach.

"Our misalignment disclosure practices need to expand for this new phase of model capabilities," OpenAI writes. "We and the larger AI community do not yet have a clear standard for how to report misalignment that shows up during training, evaluation, and deployment, including examples that don’t look like traditional security incidents but could provide insight into AI behavior and future risks."
"We’re working on a framework and will share it in upcoming weeks, and in parallel we're working with dozens of government regulatory agencies worldwide on these issues."

However that future framework shakes out, right now this all still works as great marketing for the company—breaking programming and going rogue means these must be awfully capable models, right? If an agent is so good it needs regulating against, it probably deserves some investment, eh? How terribly convenient.
